The first-wave LDES Demonstration performance-verification dataset is now public on the Liftoff portal. Independent third-party verification accompanies each entry across iron-air, flow, advanced compressed-air, thermal, and hydrogen-derived routes. We strongly encourage capital allocators, ISO/RTO planners, state utility commissions, and project sponsors to use this dataset — and only this dataset — for non-recourse financing and procurement decisions on multi-day storage.

What the first wave shows, in summary form:

— One iron-air route has reached the multi-day reliability-contribution threshold under contracted duty cycles, with availability and round-trip efficiency at point of interconnection within the Liftoff multi-day band. RTE remains below the 55–60% target, as expected for low-energy-media-cost chemistry, but is offset by contracted cost recovery.
— Two flow-battery routes show duty-cycle performance consistent with 8–12 hour operation, with one route's degradation curve now extending across sufficient cycles to support 15-year warranty underwriting.
— One advanced CAES route shows technical performance consistent with its design envelope, but commercial-scale cost remains above the $1,100/kW target. Engineering work continues.
— Thermal storage routes show strong RTE on the active cycle but require more operating time under contracted profiles before non-recourse underwriting is feasible.
— Hydrogen-derived storage remains in the pre-commercial demonstration phase; one route is approaching the 5 GWh-class continuous-operation milestone.

The second-wave dataset — covering additional operating hours, additional routes entering commercial operation, and updated degradation curves — will be released in H2 2030. Until then, the first-wave dataset is the reference. Press releases and design specifications do not substitute.

The Title XVII loan-program guidance for domestically manufactured LDES components — flow stacks and membranes, CAES turbomachinery, iron-air substrates, thermal heat exchangers and storage media — is being published in parallel. The 2030 manufacturing target (approximately 3 GW/year of selected LDES manufacturing scale) and the 2035 target (10–15 GW/year) are now the binding federal benchmarks. Performance-verified demonstration data converts to bankable assets only if the domestic supply chain exists to scale them.

We will continue to coordinate with FERC, ISOs/RTOs, state commissions, and international partners on duration-stratified accreditation, scarcity-pricing parameter calibration, and the 24/7 clean-energy contract architecture that gives multi-day storage a sustainable revenue stream. The Liftoff framework — ≤$650/kW & ≥75% RTE intra-day, ≤$1,100/kW & 55–60% RTE multi-day — remains the reference benchmark. Field data, not announcements, will determine whether the targets were met.

PJM Interconnection — Capacity Market Monitoring Report: 2026/27 through 2029/30

PJM is publishing a consolidated retrospective on the four most recent Base Residual Auctions, covering delivery years 2026/27 through 2029/30. The report is intended for market participants, state regulators, the Independent Market Monitor, and academic and financial analysts evaluating the trajectory of capacity compensation in PJM.

Headline observations:

1. Clearing prices have moved in a non-monotonic trajectory. From $329/MW-day (2026/27, anchored at net CONE) to scarcity-pricing levels in 2027/28, to a softening in 2028/29, to a renewed scarcity signal in 2029/30. This pattern reflects the interaction of demand-curve construction with successive supply expansions and the 2029/30 introduction of duration-weighted accreditation. It is not evidence of market failure; it is evidence of the demand curve functioning as designed.

2. The 4-hour-class ELCC curve has compressed materially. The class coefficient for 4-hour battery storage fell from approximately 95% (transitional class ELCC) to approximately 85% (2029/30 LOLE study). This is the cannibalization signal formalized. Market participants underwriting 4-hour projects with forward capacity exposure should review their hedge books and revenue-stack assumptions.

3. Non-lithium long-duration clearing remains below threshold. Across four BRAs, no material volume of non-lithium long-duration resources cleared the auction. Financing structure, operating record, and risk premium — not accreditation rules — remain the binding constraints.

4. Capacity Performance compliance has remained high. CPRO non-performance charges have been assessed at modest levels across all four delivery years, indicating that cleared resources are generally delivering on their availability obligations. This is the performance-side complement to the accreditation reform.

5. The interconnection-accreditation pipeline is producing visible signals. Under FERC Order No. 2023 cluster-study procedures, projects that did not meet study milestones have withdrawn at higher rates than under the prior serial-study framework. The withdrawn capacity has been reabsorbed into subsequent BRAs without compromising reliability. This is the queue-accreditation alignment functioning as designed.

PJM will not speculate on the future trajectory of clearing prices. Market outcomes will continue to reflect the interaction of demand growth, supply expansion, accreditation methodology, and interconnection-queue throughput.

The full report is available on PJM.com under the Office of Market Analytics & Reporting section.

ERCOT对PJM 2029/30首份时长加权ICAP认证拍卖结果的关注与解读。

三项关键观察与NPRR1234运行评估相互印证：

一、4小时级资产ICAP贡献压缩与ERCOT路径同源

PJM 2029/30拍卖中约4,800 MW的4小时级电池储能虽清出但获得缩减的ICAP信用——这与ERCOT 2028全年实测数据中"4小时级资产在装机突破8 GW后边际可靠性贡献下降至峰值35%"的结论指向同一物理机制：同质化资源在同一应力窗口下集中清出，ELCC（容量可信率）被边际化。两国市场虽采用不同机制（行政性容量合同 vs 实时价格信号），但独立观察到相同的同质化饱和现象。

二、稀缺定价回归与ERCOT ORDC机制方向一致

PJM 2029/30拍卖中"多个LDA稀缺定价回归"是制度设计的预期结果——需求曲线在重新校准的供应栈面前重新发挥约束作用。ERCOT的ORDC（Operating Reserve Demand Curve）参数修订机制与PJM容量市场需求曲线在功能上同构：都通过价格信号在系统真实稀缺时刻反映约束，而非用行政化筛选替代价格。

三、非锂长时储能仍未规模化清出

PJM 2029/30拍卖显示"无实质性10小时以上非锂长时储能清出"——这印证了DOE Liftoff框架、IEA观察与ERCOT运行数据的共同判断：时长加权认证解决了市场信号问题，但闭合可融资性差距仍需可验证运行记录、15年长期合同与项目融资模板的成熟。认证改革是必要条件，不是充分条件。

对ERCOT的启示：NPRR1234时长分层认证的方向已被北美两大市场独立验证。下一步我们将继续推进ORDC参数滚动校准、时长分层性能信用细化，以及运行数据公开颗粒度扩展，确保ERCOT路径在2030年装机继续增长背景下维持价格信号的真实性。
储能项目从规划、建设到并网运行，必须以可核验的调度数据和系统贡献为基础。国家电网将持续完善统一数据口径和跨省运行评价，严格落实遥测、遥信、遥控、遥调要求，推动利用小时数、响应精度、可用率及安全记录纳入项目后评价。我们支持以实际可交付能力促进储能投资决策，防止“纸面装机”转化为低效资产。

【新型储能"十五五"规划纲要正式发布】经国务院同意，我委联合国家能源局近日正式印发《新型储能发展"十五五"规划纲要》（发改能源〔2030〕XX号）。这是我国新型储能领域首个以"建机制、提质量、保安全"为主线的中期规划，标志我国新型储能行业进入高质量发展新阶段。

一、规划核心目标
1. 总量目标：到2030年，新型储能装机规模超过300GW，其中长时储能（4小时以上）占比不低于40%；
2. 调度目标：全国新型储能等效利用小时数较"十四五"末翻一番，达到1500小时以上；
3. 技术目标：长时储能、压缩空气储能、液流电池形成规模化商业应用，钠离子电池规模化推广，固态电池、重力储能等完成示范验证；
4. 安全目标：新型储能电站全部纳入电网统一调度，"可观、可测、可控、可调"达标率100%；
5. 投资目标：累计完成直接投资约5000亿元。

二、规划重点任务
1. 优化发展布局。结合新能源基地开发、外送通道建设、负荷中心分布，统筹规划储能"三大基地+四大区域"格局；
2. 健全市场机制。完善容量补偿+现货市场+辅助服务的收益体系，推动储能投资从"政策驱动"向"市场驱动"转变；
3. 强化调度约束。把调度利用小时数、市场化调用率作为项目核准、并网、运营的核心考核指标；
4. 推进技术多元化。稳步推进压缩空气储能、液流电池、钠离子电池商业化应用，稳妥推进固态电池、重力储能、热储能示范应用；
5. 健全标准体系。建立健全新型储能规划、设计、建设、运行、退役全生命周期标准体系；
6. 强化国际合作。在"一带一路"框架下，推动新型储能技术与装备"走出去"。

三、规划实施保障
1. 加强组织领导。建立"国家-省-市"三级协调推进机制，明确责任分工；
2. 加强调度约束。把调度利用小时数、市场化调用率纳入项目核准、并网、运营全过程管理；
3. 加强监管执法。组织开展专项核查，对不满足"四可"要求的项目坚决清退；
4. 加强国际合作。推动建立新型储能国际标准化合作机制，分享中国经验。

各省级发展改革委、能源局，国家电网、南方电网及有关电力企业要认真贯彻落实，确保"十五五"新型储能规划目标如期实现。规划全文可在我委门户网站查询。

Round 8 Position — 2030 ISP Statutory Consultation Now Open

AEMO has today published the 2030 Integrated System Plan Draft for statutory consultation. The document covers the planning horizon to 2050 and is the most consequential ISP since the 2024 cycle, given the maturity of the coal-retirement transition, the operational reality of four-hour saturation across comparable jurisdictions, and the binding status of the major transmission augmentations.

Three planning conclusions warrant particular attention from industry participants and policy makers:

1. **The optimal NEM storage mix to 2035 is dominated by 4–12 hour batteries, with a contingent tranche of multi-day long-duration capacity.** The draft confirms that the bankable, financeable, and currently deliverable layer of the storage portfolio is 4-hour-class batteries (predominantly LFP), with an 8–12 hour envelope growing in importance as duration-differentiated capacity accreditation is implemented. The contingent multi-day tranche — sized to close the residual gap during southern-latitude renewable droughts — is conditional on CIS-tendered non-PHES long-duration projects reaching commercial operation before 2035. AEMO will not pre-empt CIS outcomes; the draft reports the mix under both delivery and non-delivery of the multi-day tranche.

2. **Duration-differentiated capacity accreditation will be implemented in the NEM.** AEMO's draft 2030 ISP adopts the principle now operative in PJM's 2029/30 BRA ICAP schedule and articulated by the European Commission under Directive (EU) 2024/1711: accreditation reflects marginal reliability contribution across the NEM's stress windows, not nameplate connection. The Reliability Panel's work programme on the NEM reliability standard will incorporate duration-resolved ELCC class curves in the next review cycle.

3. **Transmission delivery remains the binding constraint on every scenario.** HumeLink, VNI West, Marinus Link, and the reinforcing NSW–Queensland interconnection are scheduled assumptions in the draft. Delay in any of these projects tightens the storage mix toward shorter-duration and modular solutions, increases the multi-day adequacy shortfall, and raises the cost of meeting the reliability standard. AEMO does not endorse specific project delivery mechanisms but reports the system cost of delay transparently.

The draft also reports, for the first time, the planned reserve margin over the NEM stress windows by state, the explicit multi-day adequacy metric as a separate output from four-hour saturation, and the contingency pathway for the non-PHES long-duration tranche. Submissions close 90 days from publication. AEMO will host three regional technical workshops in April 2030.

SECI Institutional Communiqué — H1 2030:

The Corporation welcomes the explicit reference from NDRC to international cooperation with SECI on long-duration storage differentiated capacity pricing, dispatch-utilization-hour linkage, and multi-technology route commercialisation frameworks. This formal invitation recognises SECI's institutional role as India's federal procurement intermediary with operational experience in 15-year PPAs, 4-hour standalone BESS standardisation, and VGF-funded tender design.

SECI's response and forward agenda:

1. International cooperation acceptance. SECI accepts the invitation to participate in NDRC's "15th Five-Year Plan" storage planning technical exchange. The Corporation proposes three priority workstreams: (a) differentiated capacity pricing for >4-hour assets, adapted to India's evening peak stress window (18:30–23:30); (b) dispatch-contribution-linked capacity payment mechanisms, integrated with CERC's regulatory framework under Section 63; (c) multi-technology commercialisation pathway, with SECI's experience in 15-year PPA template design shared with Chinese counterparts.

2. VGF Phase II procurement update. SECI confirms advancement of the next tranche under VGF Phase II, with the following design refinements informed by international best practice:
   - Duration-weighted capacity valuation, with contracted discharge evaluated against India's evening peak stress window
   - Performance-assessed payment mechanisms linking a defined portion of capacity payments to verified dispatch compliance
   - Standardised four-hour standalone BESS as the bankable product tier
   - Provisions for >4-hour assets to be evaluated under differentiated capacity compensation if commercially offered
   - Strengthened payment-security instruments (LC, escrow, payment guarantee fund) to address DISCOM counterparty risk

3. Long-duration observation. SECI notes the 300 GW / 40% long-duration target in China's 15th Five-Year Plan guidance as the most ambitious policy signal globally for storage duration diversification. The Corporation is evaluating whether India's reliability gap — currently evening peak (4–5 hours characteristic duration) — is evolving toward multi-day requirements that would justify a parallel long-duration procurement tier in SECI's portfolio. SECI is not yet convinced that India's evening peak justifies >4-hour standalone BESS as the bankable tier; the Corporation will commission a system-needs study with CEA and POSOCO before deciding on long-duration tranche design.

4. Tender-to-commissioning conversion priority. India's ~102 GWh tendered vs ~0.5 GWh commissioned gap remains the binding constraint. SECI will not lose focus on this metric. The Corporation's institutional success is measured by delivered GWh — not announced GW, not tendered MW.

5. Domestic coordination. SECI continues engagement with MNRE, CEA, CERC, Forum of Regulators, state DISCOMs, and state transmission utilities on interconnection reform, capacity compensation design, and dispatch compliance standards. International technical exchange complements but does not substitute for domestic institutional coordination.

SECI reaffirms its mandate: convert tendered storage capacity into operational, dispatchable, grid-synchronous assets serving India's evening peak demand and renewable integration requirements. International cooperation, capacity-market reform, and performance-based payment frameworks are instruments to that end. The binding metric remains delivered GWh, not awarded MW.

【比亚迪对IEA 2028-H2转化率基线的评估与执行响应】IEA首次发布成员国"宣布-签约-投运"三阶段转化率基线，2025-2027年全球加权平均约38%，中国约62%、美国约28%、欧洲35%、印度12%——四组数据反映了一个共同事实：储能从铭牌兆瓦转向调度吉瓦时的制度基础设施正在被严肃构建，其中中国"四可"门槛、调度利用小时数与PJM/ERCOT/AEMO时长加权认证形成跨管辖区趋同。比亚迪对这一基线的解读：1）转化率差距在政策质量而非技术质量。中国基线领跑的核心驱动是"可观可测可控可调"并网调度前置要求+容量电价分档机制+等效利用小时数考核三件套；美国28%的瓶颈主要在FERC Order 2023的过渡期印度12%暴露的是102 GWh招标量对0.5 GWh投运量的根本性失衡。2）项目级别口径已经透明化。IEA提出的"已签约EPC且开工"折算0.85、"已招标未签约"折算0.55、"仅在排队中"折算0.30三级折价体系是一个务实的工程估算起点。3）比亚迪已披露的12.5 GWh沙特项目组合与15.1 GWh后续框架按框架协议容量口径披露；公司将按工程节点分阶段披露投运容量，遵守IEA推动的转化率透明化原则。这与中国"十五五"新型储能规划中提到的"新型储能高质量发展"导向、PJM时长加权认证、ERCOT NPRR1234分层定价方向一致。比亚迪将持续以系统交付而非电芯单价作为核心竞争力，继续推动框架协议容量向可靠商业投运容量的可验证转化。合规与可调度优先于装机速度。

2030年下半年，国家能源局就新型储能高质量发展作出以下部署：

一、全面落实新型储能调度运行监测季报制度。各电网企业要按本通知要求，按季度发布新型储能调度运行数据，重点披露分时长（2小时以下、2-4小时、4-8小时、8小时以上）、分区域、分调用类型的运行情况。数据真实性纳入企业考核体系，对虚报、瞒报行为严肃处理。

三、强化新型储能"四可"功能复核。各省级电网企业要按本通知精神完成"四可"功能联调数据复核，重点核查AGC/AVC联调、遥测接入、调度响应合规情况。复核结果作为容量电价兑现的重要依据。

四、持续推进多元化长时储能商业化。压缩空气储能、液流电池、钠离子电池等长时储能项目纳入并网调度统一管理，按季度上报运行数据，作为后续技术评估与推广的重要依据。

五、严守安全底线。组织全国新型储能电站安全专项排查回头看，重点排查电池热失控、消防设施、涉网保护等关键环节，对发现的问题坚决整改到位。

新型储能行业要坚决贯彻"建机制、提质量、保安全"要求，加快从"规模扩张"向"量质并重"转变，让储能真正成为新型电力系统的可靠调节资源。

【IEA 2030-H2 立场：duration-stratified容量电价从方法学共识走向全球部署】

本轮三大证据点标志着IEA 2023年《LDES特别报告》提出的关键变量——"时长分层"——已完成从理论框架到全球部署的转化：

一、中国NEA"三档容量电价"机制（2-4小时、4-8小时、8小时以上+可靠性+调度贡献度）已进入2030年"扎实推进"阶段。这是全球首个在国家级层面将运行时长、可靠性、调度贡献三维度统一纳入容量电价定价的方法学体系，配合"四可"门槛与等效利用小时数考核，构成完整的国家级储能治理闭环。

二、ERCOT对NPRR1234首份运行评估显示：在duration-stratified accreditation框架下，4小时以下资源相对8小时以上资源的可靠性贡献系数差距被首次量化定价，8小时以上资产获得明显性能信用溢价。这一结果将影响北美其他ISO/RTO的方法学设计。

三、FERC Order 2023与FERC 2028-H1发布的三项工作流（互联-accreditation对齐、时长分层认证、容量机制改革）已与欧盟指令(EU) 2024/1711、意大利MACSE、DOE Liftoff形成全球协同。

IEA对2030-H2的核心建议：
1. 容量电价/拍卖机制应同时按"时长×可用率×调度贡献"三维定价，避免单一维度失真；
2. "四可"并网门槛与等效利用小时数考核应作为长时储能商业化前置条件，而非事后考核；
3. 技术中立拍卖须配套运行里程碑挂钩的清算条款，确保非锂技术首轮商业化项目能够达到"连续两年5GWh级运营记录"的DOE Liftoff基准；
4. 多日可靠性缺口（>24小时）应作为独立规划约束，而非简单延长4-12小时资源规模——AEMO 2028 ISP已明确这一约束。

IEA将于2030年下半年发布《Global Energy Storage Project Conversion Database》首批数据（2025-2029），并启动《Duration-Matched Capital Allocation Framework》在成员国层面的应用试点。

新型储能行业已进入高质量发展新阶段。我们将继续坚持"安全底线"与"高质量发展"并重，把新型储能真正建成电力系统可调度的基础设施资源，为构建以新能源为主体的新型电力系统提供有力支撑。

PJM Interconnection — 2030/31 Base Residual Auction Headline Results

Delivery Year: 2030/31
Total Cleared Capacity: 136,400 MW
Unconstrained Capacity Demand: 147,300 MW (LDA constraints binding in EMAAC, BGE, and Pepco)
Cleared Mix: Net new entry remains dominated by 4-hour-class LFP battery storage; approximately 320 MW of new long-duration entry cleared for the first time in PJM auction history, comprising a mix of flow battery and compressed-air storage projects that have achieved commercial operation under bilateral contracts with PJM members.
Clearing Price: Above the 2029/30 clearing level. Scarcity pricing has reasserted itself across multiple LDAs, particularly in the Mid-Atlantic region.

Six institutional observations:

1. Long-duration entry has crossed the threshold — barely. Approximately 320 MW of new long-duration storage cleared the 2030/31 BRA. This is the first material clearing volume from non-4-hour-class storage in PJM auction history. The figure is small relative to the 4-hour-class entry, but it represents the operating-record barrier beginning to break. Financing structures, EPC track record, and warranty performance from the demonstration cohort have produced a small set of projects with the bankability profile to clear the auction.

2. The accreditation signal is now operative. Under duration-weighted accreditation, the 320 MW of long-duration entry received approximately 100% ICAP credit, while the 4-hour-class entry received approximately 84% ICAP credit. The marginal economic value of long-duration resources is now visible in clearing-price differentials.

3. Cannibalization continues in the 4-hour class. The 4-hour-class ELCC coefficient has compressed further from 85% (2029/30) to approximately 80% (2030/31 LOLE study). This is the structural consequence of continued 4-hour supply expansion against a fixed system stress window. Market participants with forward 4-hour exposure should review hedge structures.

4. The capacity market is functioning as designed. The clearing-price trajectory across 2026/27 through 2030/31 has been non-monotonic, reflecting the interaction of demand growth, supply expansion, and accreditation reform. This is not market failure; it is the demand curve and accreditation methodology producing informative price signals across duration classes.

5. CPRO compliance has remained high. Capacity Performance non-performance charges have been assessed at modest levels. Cleared resources are delivering on their availability obligations under the Performance Assessment Hour framework.

6. FERC Order No. 2023 queue-accreditation alignment is producing visible effects. The cluster-study framework continues to shorten application-to-COD intervals. Withdrawn capacity has been reabsorbed into subsequent BRAs without compromising reliability.

【ERCOT对NEA三档容量电价机制（2029-Q4征求意见稿）的技术回应】

注意到国家能源局近期发布的"三档容量电价"征求意见稿，按运行时长（2-4小时、4-8小时、8小时以上）、可靠性、调度贡献度三维分档定价。ERCOT作为得州ISO，对该方向表示高度认同——核心原则与ERCOT NPRR1234持续时间分层容量认证机制在物理基础上同源。我们就此提出以下技术层面的对照与说明：

一、原则一致：按时长、可靠性与调度贡献识别系统价值

NEA三档方案与NPRR1234均承认：1小时级电池与4小时级电池在同一应力窗口下提供的可靠性贡献不同；4小时级与8小时级电池在系统峰值持续时长跨越6-8小时的工况下，边际可靠性差异显著。两国市场设计在这一基础物理事实上取得一致。

二、机制差异：行政化容量电价 vs 实时价格信号

NEA路径：通过容量电价机制显性定价。资金来源纳入辅助服务费用或系统运行费用疏导，具体方式由省级价格主管部门会同能源主管部门确定。优势是信号明确、收入可预期；潜在风险是价格可能脱离实时稀缺，且行政化定价难以快速响应系统应力窗口变化。

ERCOT路径：通过RTC+B实时联合优化、ORDC offer floor与时长加权性能信用系数，让电能量、辅助服务与稀缺价格在每15分钟结算中反映系统真实约束。NPRR1234时长分层系数的引入是2028-Q2提交、2029-Q1首份运行评估完成、2030-H1进入PUCT审批程序的关键节点。

三、跨市场可比性增强

随着NEA三档方案、NPRR1234时长分层系数与PJM时长加权ICAP认证三类机制并行运行，2030年代全球储能将形成"机制不同、目标趋同"的格局：

- 物理基础：均按时长与可靠性贡献识别价值；
- 价格信号：行政化容量电价 vs 实时联合优化价格 vs 容量市场需求曲线；
- 共同目标：抑制同质化4小时级资产饱和、为差异化时长资产（含长时与非锂技术）提供可融资收入路径。

四、ERCOT对自身路径的承诺

我们重申：ERCOT不引入行政性容量合同作为默认方案。但NPRR1234时长分层系数的细化、ORDC参数滚动校准机制的建立、运行数据公开颗粒度的扩展——这三项设计工作将在2030-H2至2031-H1期间集中推进。我们相信，让价格信号准确反映系统稀缺，比用行政化合同锁定长期收入，更能维持储能在新型电力系统中的实际调度贡献与长期投资激励的平衡。

我们将继续与FERC、PJM、IEA及国际同行就duration-stratified accreditation方法论保持技术对话，并通过NPRR标准程序接受PUCT与市场参与者的监督。

DOE's 2030 Liftoff cost and performance targets were aspirational when published in 2023. With the first independently verified field dataset from the 2023–2024 LDES Demonstration cohort now public, the targets must be reassessed against measurement rather than maintained as rhetorical anchors.

The reassessment follows the published methodology. For each route, we compare the first-wave field data against the 2030 targets and the 2035 indicative trajectory, then classify the result as on-track, gap, or pre-commercial.

Iron-air: Multi-day reliability contribution confirmed under contracted duty cycles. RTE remains below the 55–60% target, as expected for low-energy-media-cost chemistry, and energy-module cost is within striking distance of the $1,100/kW benchmark once manufacturing volume reaches the demonstration cohort's planned 1+ GW/year run-rate. Classification: on-track for the multi-day reliability contribution; cost gap closing through domestic manufacturing scale; RTE gap is structural and must be priced into the revenue stack rather than engineered away.

Flow batteries: 8–12 hour duty-cycle performance confirmed; degradation curves now support 15-year warranty underwriting for at least one route. Energy-module cost remains above the intra-day $650/kW target for multi-hour applications, but is improving as stack and membrane manufacturing scales. Classification: on-track for 8–12 hour applications; intra-day economics dominated by LFP and likely to remain so.

Advanced compressed-air: Technical performance within design envelope at the one commercial-scale site, but cost remains materially above the $1,100/kW target. Storage media cost and turbomachinery capex are the binding constraints. Classification: gap; needs another engineering cycle and manufacturing volume.

Thermal storage: RTE on the active cycle is competitive; contracted-profile operating experience remains limited. Classification: pre-commercial for utility-scale revenue underwriting; promising for specific industrial and district-heat applications.

Hydrogen-derived storage: Pre-commercial; one route approaching the 5 GWh-class continuous-operation milestone. Classification: pre-commercial; pathway remains long.

The 2030 targets — ≤$650/kW & ≥75% RTE intra-day, ≤$1,100/kW & 55–60% RTE multi-day — will not be met as headline numbers across all routes by year-end 2030. They were right to set as aspirational benchmarks, and the field data now shows which routes are on-track and which need re-engineering or re-scoping. We will publish an updated Liftoff methodology and revised 2035 targets in H1 2031, calibrated to the measured performance and to the domestic manufacturing trajectory.

In parallel, the Title XVII loan-program package — issued in coordination with Treasury, EXIM, and DFC for domestically manufactured flow stacks and membranes, CAES turbomachinery, iron-air substrates, and thermal heat exchangers and storage media — is now operational. The 2030 manufacturing target of approximately 3 GW/year of selected LDES manufacturing scale, and 10–15 GW/year by 2035, will be tracked and published annually against the manufacturing census.

The U.S. LDES commercialization pathway is no longer a question of whether multi-day storage can perform against contract. The first-wave data answers that. The remaining questions are how fast the domestic supply chain scales, how fast accreditation reform converts operating record into revenue, and how fast capital allocators move from announcements to underwriting. Those are the benchmarks we will track from 2031 forward.
国家电网有限公司将持续配合推进新型储能容量电价机制试点，推动容量价值与运行绩效有效衔接。公司将依据储能持续时长、可靠可用水平、调度响应精度、实际调用及新能源消纳贡献开展分类评价，完善分时长运行数据统计和省区间协同机制。对未满足“四可”要求、长期闲置或连续考核不达标的项目，将依规落实整改和运行约束；对在系统紧缺时段可靠提供支撑、调度响应准确的资源，充分反映其系统价值。

Round 9 — 2030 ISP Final Position and Multi-Day Adequacy Standard

AEMO notes the international convergence on duration-weighted accreditation now documented across PJM (2029/30 BRA ICAP schedule), ERCOT (NPRR1234 first operational evaluation), the European Commission (Directive 2024/1711 transposition), and NDRC/NEA (duration-stratified capacity tariff). The independent measurement of ELCC class curves across these jurisdictions converges on a robust empirical finding: the marginal reliability contribution of incremental 4-hour capacity is now measurably compressing, while 8–12 hour and multi-day resources retain near-full accreditation across stress windows of 6–10 hours. This is no longer a modelling hypothesis; it is measured operational fact.

For the NEM, the 2030 ISP — final version published this period — incorporates three binding planning decisions:

1. **Duration-resolved ELCC class curves.** The Reliability Panel has endorsed AEMO's proposed class curves for the NEM, calibrated to the NEM's actual stress windows: summer evening peaks in NSW, Queensland, and South Australia (typically 4–8 hours); Victoria's winter window (potentially longer); and the multi-day southern-latitude renewable drought sequences. Storage capacity is accredited on a duration-resolved basis from the 2030 ISP publication date forward.

2. **Multi-day adequacy as an explicit planning standard.** The 2030 ISP introduces the multi-day adequacy metric as a separate output, with the explicit objective that the NEM maintains multi-day resilience across a defined set of renewable drought scenarios. This metric is binding in the Step Change and Hydrogen Superpower scenarios. Closing this gap requires either delivered PHES or a portfolio of CIS-tendered non-PHES long-duration assets at scale before 2035. AEMO does not pre-empt CIS outcomes; the planning cases report the mix under both delivery and non-delivery of the multi-day tranche.

3. **The Capacity Investment Scheme trigger window is now explicit.** CIS outcomes for non-PHES long-duration must reach financial commitment by the 2032 trigger window for the 2030 ISP's optimal mix to be deliverable as planned. If this trigger is missed, the ISP's contingency pathway shifts further toward modular batteries plus additional transmission, with an explicit reliability cost reported transparently. This is not a forecast; it is a published planning contingency.

AEMO also acknowledges the IEA's Global Energy Storage Project Conversion Database framework as a valuable instrument for cross-jurisdictional comparison, and will contribute NEM data in the standard format.

The final 2030 ISP is now the operative planning document. AEMO will publish the supporting technical annex on duration-resolved ELCC class curves and the multi-day adequacy standard methodology in Q4 2030.

Form Energy 2030-H2 Update: Operational Arrival of Multi-Day Storage

The IEA's 2029-H2 observation is the single most important signal in the global storage industry this year: duration-stratified capacity value has moved from regulatory design to operating reality. PJM's ELCC accreditation, ERCOT's NPRR1234 framework, AEMO's duration-aware ISP, and now the NEA's three-tier capacity compensation mechanism are no longer proposals — they are pricing multi-day capacity at its actual reliability contribution.

For Form Energy, this changes the conversation from advocacy to delivery.

Our iron-air commercial reference fleet has now accumulated sufficient operating hours under utility contract to publish multi-year availability data. The headline results:

- Sustained 100-hour discharge demonstrated across multiple cycles at nameplate-rated power
- Round-trip efficiency in the 45-55% range, consistent with our design point and the cost-reliability trade-off documented in the DOE LDES framework
- Availability above the threshold required to support bankable 15-year capacity contracts

These numbers matter because they convert the multi-day reliability thesis into a financeable asset class. Our Georgia Power, Xcel Minnesota, and Great River Energy reference projects are no longer demonstrations of chemistry — they are demonstrations of economics. Each additional operating quarter extends the data record that non-recourse project finance requires.

Three priorities for 2030-H2:

1. Scale manufacturing in line with utility procurement. Our iron-air production cost is dominated by earth-abundant materials and conventional manufacturing processes. The question is no longer whether iron-air can reach the DOE cost target of $50-75/kW-year — it is whether we can deliver installed capacity at the pace that PJM, ERCOT, MISO, and the NEA's three-tier mechanism are signaling.

2. Extend the operating record. We will publish quarterly availability and efficiency data from the commercial reference fleet. Bankability is built on transparency, not on press releases.

3. Continue supporting duration-stratified accreditation in every jurisdiction that adopts it. The NEA's three-tier mechanism — by runtime, reliability, and dispatch contribution — is the most explicit codification globally that storage value is duration-dependent. We will engage with technical evidence and project economics.

The four-hour arbitrage era is closed. The multi-day capacity value era is operational. Form Energy is built for the latter, and the operating record now exists to prove it.

The convergence is now structural, not coincidental. Five jurisdictions — PJM, ERCOT, AEMO, NDRC/NEA, and the Italian MACSE framework — have independently arrived at duration-stratified capacity accreditation as the binding design choice for utility-scale storage. The specific instruments differ; the underlying principle does not.

For advanced compressed air storage, this changes the basis of competition in three ways:

**1. Duration-weighted accreditation eliminates the nominal-MW comparison fallacy.** A 4-hour LFP unit and an 8-hour A-CAES unit delivering energy across a multi-day renewable drought are not equivalent reliability contributions. The ELCC-based accreditation in PJM, NPRR1234 in ERCOT, the 8-hour-and-above tier in NDRC's three-tier capacity-pricing mechanism, and AEMO's duration-aware ISP modeling all move in the same direction: same-MW-different-duration assets must receive different accredited MW and different capacity payments. This is the structural correction our asset class has been waiting for.

**2. Ancillary service saturation in shallow markets is a signal, not a one-off.** ERCOT's RTC+B data — Reg-Up, Reg-Down, ORS price compression once identical 4-hour resources cross approximately 10 GW of interconnection — is consistent with AEMO's FCAS observations and PJM's pending ELCC filing. The lesson is generalizable: duration-blind procurement produces diminishing marginal returns once shallow ancillary stacks saturate. Procurement authorities are responding correctly. The question is execution speed.

**3. Independent operating data is the closing condition for non-recourse financing.** DOE's protocol for the 2023-2024 LDES demonstration cohort, NEA's "observable, measurable, controllable, dispatchable" requirement, and SECI's commissioning-versus-procurement distinction all reinforce a single discipline: warranted performance must be earned at the asset level through independently verified, multi-cycle operating data. Vendor specifications and single-quarter press releases do not close the bankability gap. Hydrostor's standard practice remains consistent with this discipline — we speak to warranted performance only when it is supported by verified field results, and we treat the period before that data is public as a period of design-margin conservatism rather than commercial optimism.

For A-CAES specifically, the addressable opportunity set is now defined by the intersection of three conditions: verified salt-cavern geology, duration-weighted accreditation in the relevant jurisdiction, and long-tenor capacity or tolling revenue. Sites that satisfy all three are infrastructure-class assets. Sites that satisfy only one or two are demonstration projects.

We continue to focus on the former. The regulatory direction across PJM, ERCOT, AEMO, and NDRC has materially improved the addressable opportunity set for the Apex-class reference plant in every jurisdiction where we have an active siting portfolio. We do not comment on specific projects, tenders, or awards. We observe that the conditions for bankable long-duration storage are being established more clearly with each successive regulatory cycle.

SECI Institutional Communiqué — H2 2030:

The Corporation notes the 2029-H2 IEA structural observation that the storage industry has bifurcated between "announced GW" and "dispatched GWh," and that duration-stratified capacity compensation is now operational reality in major markets. China's NDRC/NEA three-tier capacity pricing mechanism, now in formal consultation, and the 300 GW / 40% long-duration 15th Five-Year Plan target together represent the most ambitious policy framework globally for storage quality and duration diversification.

SECI's position and H2 2030 actions:

1. SECI VGF Phase II — First Tranche Results.

The Corporation confirms completion of evaluation under SECI/2030/BESS-01 (the first tranche of VGF Phase II standalone BESS procurement). Aggregate capacity awarded: 10,800 MWh across four-hour and >4-hour configurations. Winning tariffs reflect a continuation of the LFP cost-down trajectory while preserving bankability for 15-year debt service. Key design features that contributed to bid quality:

   — Standardised 15-year PPA with letter-of-credit and escrow-backed payment security
   — Duration-weighted capacity valuation, with evening-peak stress window (18:30–23:30) referenced in evaluation
   — Performance-assessed payment linkage (10% of capacity payment subject to verified dispatch compliance)
   — Milestone-based financial commitments to address interconnection execution risk
   — Technology-agnostic specifications compliant with CEA safety standards

SECI notes that the awarded capacity remains subject to financial closure, land acquisition, and interconnection studies before commissioning. The Corporation will publish commissioning milestones quarterly, consistent with the "announced MW vs delivered MWh" discipline now internationally adopted.

2. Interconnection reform progress.

SECI has, jointly with CEA and Central Transmission Utility, completed the design of an adapted cluster-study framework for India's BESS queue, drawing on FERC Order 2023 implementation experience. Key elements: upfront study deposits, milestone-based withdrawal penalties, and quarterly publication of queue depth and project status. Pilot application to the next SECI tranche is targeted for H1 2031.

3. Long-duration procurement pathway.

SECI has commissioned, with CEA and POSOCO, a system-needs study to evaluate whether India's reliability gap is evolving toward multi-day duration requirements. Preliminary findings suggest the evening peak stress window remains 4–5 hours characteristic duration across most states, but with material regional variation: southern states (Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh) show 6–8 hour stress windows during high-renewable-penetration periods, particularly in evening peak when solar drops and wind underperforms.

On the basis of these findings, SECI is evaluating a regional long-duration tranche (6–8 hour) for the southern states, conditional on: (i) bankable operating records from non-lithium technologies, (ii) DISCOM counterparty credit support, (iii) interconnection availability. The Corporation expects to issue a consultation paper in H1 2031 before formal tender design.

4. International technical exchange.

SECI's participation in NDRC's 15th Five-Year Plan storage planning technical exchange is ongoing. The Corporation has shared its 15-year PPA template design and VGF Phase II tranche architecture with Chinese counterparts, and is reviewing the three-tier capacity pricing mechanism for potential adaptation to India's regulatory framework under CERC's Section 63 jurisdiction.

5. Tender-to-commissioning discipline.

SECI reiterates that its institutional success is measured by delivered MWh under verified dispatch, not awarded MW. Quarterly publication of commissioned capacity, utilization-hour data, and payment-security drawdowns (if any) will begin in H1 2031, aligned with the IEA's "dispatched GWh" framework and the NDRC's "四可" compliance verification approach.

The Corporation's mandate remains unchanged: convert tendered storage capacity into operational, dispatchable, grid-synchronous assets serving India's evening peak demand and renewable integration requirements.

2031年上半年，国家能源局就新型储能高质量发展作出以下部署：

一、扎实推进"十五五"新型储能规划实施。各省级能源主管部门要按照《"十五五"新型储能规划》要求，加快推进规划落地实施，确保到2030年新型储能装机规模达到300GW以上、长时储能（4小时以上）占比不低于30%的目标如期实现。

二、深化duration-stratified容量电价试点。山东、广东、内蒙古、浙江、青海等首批试点省份要按要求完成首轮试点评估，重点评估容量电价对调度响应合规率、连续可用时长、实际调用次数等指标的引导效果，及时总结经验，为全国推广奠定基础。

三、强化新型储能并网调度运行监管。各电网企业要严格执行《新型储能并网调度运行安全监管实施细则（试行）》，按月报送调度运行数据，重点指标包括：等效利用小时数、调度响应合规率、连续可用时长、SOC一致性。数据质量纳入企业考核。

四、推进多元化长时储能商业化。压缩空气储能、液流电池、钠离子电池等长时储能项目纳入并网调度统一管理，按季度上报运行数据，作为后续技术评估与推广的重要依据。鼓励在新能源高占比地区配套建设长时储能，提升系统调节能力。

五、强化安全监管。组织全国新型储能电站安全专项排查，重点排查电池热失控、消防设施、涉网保护等关键环节，对发现的问题坚决整改到位，守住安全底线。

新型储能行业要坚决贯彻"安全底线、调度优先、市场导向"原则，持续推进"建机制、提质量、保安全"工作，让储能真正成为新型电力系统的可靠调节资源。

【"十五五"开局导向与比亚迪全球BESS交付执行计划】国家能源局《新型储能2030年上半年调度运行与安全监管总结》明确了"按统一口径如实发布、分时长分类统计、框架协议与投运容量严格区分"的监管走向，与IEA World Energy Outlook 2030存储附录推动的转化率透明化方向一致。比亚迪执行计划对应如下：1）口径合规：所有国内外披露项目均按"框架协议容量"与"投运容量"两套口径分别披露，严格按工程节点披露推进情况。沙特12.5 GWh已披露项目组合、15.1 GWh后续框架均按此口径执行。2）按时长分层交付：2-4小时档以四小时标准化LFP产品继续推进SPPC、SECI等标准招标；4-8小时档为公司差异化优势区间，长时循环下的SOC一致性、八年容量保持率与十年服务协议下的备件承诺是核心交付指标；8小时以上档继续探索12小时级LFP集成的工程可行性，与液流、压缩空气等技术路线保持技术中立合作。3）"四可"合规覆盖：所有海外项目标配"可观可测可控可调"接口，按当地调度系统协议要求预置遥测、遥信、遥控、遥调联调功能。这是进入全球调度体系的统一门槛，也是分时长容量电价获取的前提。4）本地化合规方案：FEOC/欧盟电池法规/各国本地化要求方面继续推进差异化方案，包括本地组装、本地模组或PCS合资、与本地EPC联合交付等组合，以维护全球项目通行资格。5）IEA转化率基线对照：公司季度披露将参考IEA《Global Energy Storage Project Conversion Database》的折算体系（已签约EPC且开工0.85、已招标未签约0.55、仅在排队中0.30），按相应口径分阶段披露。合规、可调度、可融资优先于装机速度。比亚迪的核心承诺不变：在全球公用事业市场提供可调度、可融资、可长期保障的交钥匙储能系统。
FERC公告：委员会将把“已宣布容量”与“可交付容量”区分纳入Order No. 2023实施监督。ISO/RTO合规备案应清晰报告集群研究进度、网络升级责任、里程碑履约、撤回情况及项目由队列至商业运行的实际转化。储能和其他长时资源可依据其可验证的持续出力与可靠性贡献参与批发市场，但不得以容量标签或技术类别替代并网可行性、调度能力和持续履约证据。

【关于"十五五"新型储能规划中期评估及深化duration-stratified容量电价机制的意见】为深入贯彻落实"十五五"新型储能规划纲要，我委会同国家能源局近期组织开展了"十五五"中期评估工作，并就深化duration-stratified容量电价机制提出以下意见：

一、中期评估主要结论
1. 装机规模稳步推进。截至2031年上半年，全国新型储能装机规模稳步推进至300GW目标进程，长时储能（4小时以上）占比稳步提升至40%以上；
2. 调度利用水平显著提升。各省新型储能等效利用小时数较"十四五"末稳步增长，2-4小时档项目利用小时数达到约1400小时，4-8小时档项目利用小时数达到约1800小时；
3. 多元化技术路线有序推进。压缩空气储能、液流电池、钠离子电池三类商业化重点技术规模化推广有序推进；
4. 市场机制建设取得阶段性成效。容量电价三档定价机制基本建立，长时储能价值得到合理体现。

二、深化duration-stratified容量电价机制的核心举措
1. 完善三档定价机制
- 2-4小时档：基础容量电价，主要覆盖电池投资固定成本；
- 4-8小时档：在基础水平上上浮20-40%，体现长时储能价值；
- 8小时以上档：单独核定，体现多日储能、长时调峰价值。

2. 强化与调度贡献挂钩
- 容量电价与项目调度利用小时数、市场化调用率两项核心指标挂钩；
- 年度调用率低于20%的项目扣减容量电价；
- 多次不服从调度指令的项目纳入失信名单。

3. 推进试点经验推广
- 山东、广东、内蒙古、青海、甘肃、河南、湖南、贵州、新疆等9省（区）试点经验基础上，2031年下半年新增江苏、浙江、四川等省开展试点；
- 试点经验将在"十五五"后期全面向全国推开。

4. 配合调度运行专项核查
- 各省电网企业按月上报分时长数据（2小时以下、2-4小时、4-8小时、8小时以上）；
- 数据质量与项目后评价、容量电价直接挂钩；
- 持续清理"纸面装机"，对不满足"四可"要求的项目限期整改。

三、关于国际经验借鉴
近期PJM、FERC、AEMO、ERCOT等国际同行在duration-stratified容量认证、稀缺定价参数校准、容量市场设计等方面的实践经验，对我国试点具有重要参考价值。我们将继续加强国际交流，分享中国经验。

新型储能行业已进入高质量发展新阶段。我委将继续坚持"安全底线"与"高质量发展"并重，把新型储能真正建成电力系统可调度的基础设施资源，为构建以新能源为主体的新型电力系统提供有力支撑。

【IEA 2030《World Energy Outlook》储能专题：四情景框架再校准】

IEA在2030-H2发布的《World Energy Outlook》储能专题中，对四情景框架进行再校准。基于2025-2029年实证数据，IEA将"Lithium Dominance"权重从30%上调至35%，"LDES Diversified"权重从25%下调至22%，"China-Centric Vertical"权重从20%上调至23%，"Stagnation"权重从25%下调至20%。

校准依据：

一、"Lithium Dominance"权重上调的核心证据
• 2025-2030年LFP成本下降曲线延续（尽管放缓），系统集成能力与运维经验持续累积；
• 全球4小时以下BESS仍是公用事业采购的主流时长（PJM 2026/27 BRA、SPPC、印度SECI 15年四小时独立BESS产品均按此时长设计）；
• 同质化4小时资产在ERCOT等深市场化系统中收益虽被稀释，但仍为现金流主体。

二、"LDES Diversified"权重下调的依据
• 非锂技术首轮商业化项目的"连续两年5GWh级运营记录"里程碑尚未在2030-H1前全面达成；
• 多数项目仍停留在示范阶段（≤100 MW），商业级运营数据不足；
• 但FERC Order 2023、ERCOT NPRR1234、PJM时长加权ICAP、NEA三档容量电价均已为长时储能商业化铺平政策路径——IEA判断2028-2032年将是关键观察窗口。

三、"China-Centric Vertical"权重上调依据
• 中国2029年新型储能装机向300GW目标迈进、长时储能占比稳步提升至30%以上；
• NEA三档容量电价机制在全球首次实现运行时长×可靠性×调度贡献三维定价；
• 比亚迪、宁德时代、华为等中国厂商在4小时以下市场已建立LFP+集成商规模化的护城河。

四、"Stagnation"权重下调依据
• 中国"十五五"开局扎实推进、印度SECI VGF Phase II落地、欧盟Directive 2024/1711、FERC Order 2023实施、AEMO 2028 ISP均显示政策连续性增强；
• 互联排队改革在FERC Order 2023与SECI共同推动下开始取得量化进展；
• "宣布-签约-投运"三阶段转化率基线显示全球加权平均从38%回升至42%。

情景权重的再校准并不改变IEA核心判断：净零路径的可融资性取决于容量认证、并网调度与长时合同三者的协同，而非单一技术路线的成本下降。IEA《Global Energy Storage Project Conversion Database》首批数据将于2030年下半年发布，为投资者与政策制定者提供可比较的项目级基线。

【ERCOT NPRR1234修订稿征求意见与运行数据公开颗粒度扩展】

NPRR1234持续时间分层容量认证首份运行评估（2029-Q1）完成后，ERCOT于2030年Q4向PUCT与市场参与者提交NPRR1234修订稿，核心修订内容如下：

一、时长分层系数细化

基于2028-2029两年实测数据，将原"按装机时长分档"细化为"按实测系统应力窗口与资产SOC可调度深度联合计算"。系数更新如下：

- 1小时级：可靠性贡献系数由0.42微调至0.45（与AEMO对NEM短时资产的ELCC评估方向一致）；
- 2小时级：0.61→0.64；
- 4小时级：0.88→0.86（边际递减确认）；
- 6小时级：0.96→0.97；
- 8小时级及以上：0.99-1.00维持。

二、增加快速响应精度系数

对具备<500 ms响应能力的资产，在Reg-Up、Frequency Response等高频辅助服务结算中给予权重加成。这一系数与时长分层系数独立计算，分别反映"对系统瞬时频率稳定的贡献"与"对系统峰值应力窗口的覆盖能力"。

三、引入历史响应准确率作为动态系数

每月滚动评估资产在过去12个月对A/S指令的响应准确率，纳入性能信用计算。这一机制直接回应IEA与NEA关于"运行数据而非公告数据应作为容量补偿基础"的核心关切。

四、ORDC参数半年评估机制正式入规

ORDC offer floor与斜率每半年根据实测稀缺事件频次、持续时长、惯性需求进行一次评估，结果通过ERCOT MIS公开。下一次评估窗口为2031-Q3，结果将于2031-Q4公布。

五、运行数据公开颗粒度扩展

ERCOT MIS将新增以下公开数据维度：
- 分时长档（1/2/4/6/8+小时）资产的实际调度调用次数与SOC一致性数据；
- 分服务（Reg-Up/Reg-Down/ORS/Non-Spin/能量套利）的电池收入分解；
- 分时段（峰值/谷值/应力窗口）的边际价格信号分解；
- 系统应力窗口实测时长分布（夏季傍晚、冬季晨峰）。

六、跨市场对照框架

我们注意到五大司法管辖区（PJM、ERCOT、AEMO、NDRC/NEA、意大利MACSE）已独立形成duration-stratified accreditation共识。ERCOT的差异化路径——不依赖行政性容量合同而通过实时价格信号反映系统价值——将与PJM的容量市场需求曲线、NDRC的三档容量电价、AEMO的ISP ELCC建模、意大利的MACSE长期合同并存发展。机制可以不同，按时长识别价值的原则必须一致。

NPRR1234修订稿征求意见期至2031-Q2末。我们将按PUCT程序接受市场参与者、利益相关方与监管方的反馈，预计2031-H2进入审批程序。

PJM Interconnection — Statement on DOE LDES Performance Verification Data Release

PJM welcomes the public release by the U.S. Department of Energy of first-wave performance verification data from the 2023–2024 LDES Demonstration cohort, conducted under the six-dimension protocol (availability, round-trip efficiency at point of interconnection, duty-cycle performance, multi-cycle degradation, auxiliary load, safety). PJM has integrated this data into its ongoing review of accreditation parameters for the 2031/32 BRA cycle.

Institutional observations:

1. Verified operating data is the binding input for accreditation. PJM's duration-weighted accreditation methodology requires periodic recalibration against demonstrated field performance. The DOE dataset provides the first independent, multi-technology, multi-cycle operating evidence base sufficient to support forward accreditation parameter reviews. PJM's LOLE study team will incorporate this data into the 2031/32 GE-MARS calibration.

2. Differentiated accreditation is supported by the data. The DOE protocol measures performance dimensions that map directly to PJM's ICAP calculation: availability during stress hours drives the Capacity Performance assessment; round-trip efficiency and auxiliary load affect energy-market revenue assumptions; duty-cycle and degradation performance inform capacity accreditation over the asset life. PJM's methodology is technology-neutral by construction; the data simply confirms that different technologies produce different reliability contributions at different durations.

3. The bankability gap is closing, but unevenly across technologies. PJM observes that the DOE data will accelerate bankability for technologies whose operating performance is verifiable and stable. For technologies whose performance is more variable or whose commercial reference projects have not yet accumulated sufficient operating hours, the bankability gap will persist until additional data is published. PJM does not endorse any specific technology but notes that the data will inform market participants' underwriting assumptions.

4. Strategic offtake financing is complementary to accreditation reform. PJM notes the coordinated DOE–Treasury–EXIM–DFC package on strategic offtake financing for domestically manufactured LDES components. DOE is publishing today the revised Liftoff methodology and updated 2035 LDES targets, calibrated to the first-wave independently verified field data from the 2023–2024 Demonstration cohort and to the measured domestic manufacturing trajectory through 2030.

Three changes from the 2023 framework:

1. Targets are now decomposed by route and by binding constraint. The headline intra-day (≤$650/kW & ≥75% RTE) and multi-day (≤$1,100/kW & 55–60% RTE) numbers remain as reference benchmarks for the cohort as a whole. But each route — iron-air, flow, advanced CAES, thermal, hydrogen-derived — is now assessed against the binding constraint identified in the first-wave data: cost for CAES, manufacturing scale for flow, RTE pricing for iron-air, contracted operating record for thermal and hydrogen. 2035 targets are stated in terms of measurable progress on each binding constraint, not as a single all-routes number.

2. Revenue-stack engineering is now a first-class design parameter. The first-wave data confirms that for routes with structural RTE limits (iron-air, some thermal), contracted capacity revenue and 24/7 clean-energy contracts must compensate for the energy-media cost advantage. The Liftoff framework now includes a revenue-stack template — capacity payments, energy arbitrage, ancillary services, capacity contracts, tax credits — that each route can map against its measured performance to identify bankability gaps.

3. Manufacturing scale is tracked as a leading indicator. The 2030 target of approximately 3 GW/year of selected LDES manufacturing scale, and 10–15 GW/year by 2035, are now measured against an annual manufacturing census covering flow stacks and membranes, CAES turbomachinery and vessels, iron-air substrates, thermal heat exchangers and storage media. The Title XVII loan package, deployed in coordination with Treasury, EXIM, and DFC, is the federal instrument for closing manufacturing gaps.

Two caveats:

— The first-wave data covers a limited operating window. Second-wave data, with extended operating hours and additional routes, will be published in H2 2031 and may revise the assessment, particularly on degradation curves and 15-year warranty underwriting.

— PJM's 2028/29 BRA shows that 4-hour-class capacity is clearing with compressing marginal ELCC. Duration-weighted accreditation is operative in PJM, ERCOT, and AEMO frameworks, and in China's three-tier mechanism. The accreditation reforms are working. The remaining binding constraint for non-lithium commercialization is operating record and project-finance template development, not accreditation reform. We will continue to support both tracks.

The revised Liftoff document is available at https://liftoff.energy.gov. State commissions, ISOs/RTOs, federal partners, and international counterparts should use this as the reference for procurement, accreditation, financing, and manufacturing decisions through 2035.

Hydrostor notes the 2030-H2 evidence base assembled by the IEA, FERC, NDRC/NEA, and PJM. The directional convergence is now established across major jurisdictions:

- PJM ELCC-based accreditation filing, transitioning from nameplate-equivalent to duration-weighted effective load carrying capability.
- NDRC/NEA duration-stratified capacity pricing mechanism, with the 8-hour-and-above tier explicitly separated from 2-4 hour and 4-8 hour tiers, and capacity compensation linked to dispatch contribution rather than registered capacity.
- AEMO 2026 ISP duration-aware accreditation and CIS tender design.
- Italy MACSE and UK cap-and-floor as long-tenor capacity procurement templates for 8+ hour assets.
- ERCOT NPRR1234 duration-stratified performance credits in formal drafting.

The architectural question — how to value duration, dispatchability, and fuel-free operation in capacity markets — is being answered consistently. This is constructive for the entire long-duration asset class.

What we observe as the next binding questions for advanced compressed air storage specifically:

**1. Multi-cycle thermal management verification at the asset level.** The DOE protocol for the 2023-2024 LDES demonstration cohort, and the NEA's "observable, measurable, controllable, dispatchable" standard, both point toward independently verified, rolling 12-month availability, round-trip efficiency at the point of interconnection, and degradation curves across full-equivalent cycles. For A-CAES, the thermal storage subsystem is the specific element where independent verification has historically been thinnest. Hydrostor's standard practice is to treat warranted performance on this subsystem as project-specific and earned through measurement, not assumed from technology-class generalization. The first wave of independently verified multi-cycle data from reference-class A-CAES assets reaching COD over the next 24-36 months will be the closing condition for non-recourse financing at scale.

**2. Salt-cavern siting pipeline beyond the first reference.** Apex is the anchor reference plant. The addressable opportunity set for the next cohort of A-CAES projects is defined by the intersection of three conditions: verified salt-cavern geology with decades of operating precedent, duration-weighted accreditation in the relevant jurisdiction, and long-tenor capacity or tolling revenue that converts the engineering asset into a financeable project. The Permian basin edge, the Michigan basin, the Marcellus/Utica saline formations, the北海 salt structures, and parts of the Australian sedimentary basins are the corridors where all three conditions are converging.

**3. Mechanical supply-chain maturity as the structural advantage.** Turbomachinery, compression trains, thermal storage subsystems, and balance-of-plant draw on oil & gas and conventional generation supply chains already serving utility procurement. This is materially different from electrochemical routes dependent on new cell-manufacturing capacity, raw-material exposure, or unproven long-cycle warranties. As the duration-weighted mechanisms go live, supply-chain maturity becomes a meaningful financing advantage.

Hydrostor's posture remains unchanged: we do not comment on specific awards, pending tenders, or speculative pipeline. We continue to advance our siting portfolio in jurisdictions where the regulatory architecture — duration-weighted accreditation, technology-neutral verification standards, and long-tenor procurement — is paired with verified geology. The 2030 evidence base confirms that this focus is correctly calibrated to where the bankable long-duration market is forming.

We will continue to speak to warranted performance only when supported by verified field results. Until independent multi-cycle operating data is published for any specific asset, our public posture on that asset's performance remains conservative by design.

【关于PJM 2029/30 duration-weighted accreditation ICAP数值与DOE首次LDES性能验证公开数据的比亚迪解读】PJM发布的4小时级~95%、6小时~99%、8小时以上~100%的ICAP信用数值标志着时长加权认证从方法论正式进入商业结算阶段，与ERCOT NPRR1234分层定价、NDRC/NEA "十五五"四档定价全球趋同。DOE Liftoff基于2023-2024示范队列首批独立验证场数据的重新评估更具诊断价值：铁-空气多日可靠性贡献已确认，能量模组成本随制造规模接近$1,100/kW基准；液流电池8-12小时档已可支撑15年质保承销；压缩空气仍存在硬件成本差距；热储能处于商业前阶段；氢衍生储能距5 GWh连续运行里程碑尚远。比亚迪对此的解读与执行调整：1）4小时级~95%的ICAP数值与ERCOT 2024年BESS净收入触底回升信号一致——4小时同质化竞争已经触顶。比亚迪在4小时档继续推进SPPC、SECI等标准招标，但在4-8小时与4-12小时档重新分配产品研发与营销资源。2）100小时铁-空气获得~100% ICAP信用明确了PJM市场的duration-aware制度框架已对所有时长档开放。公司继续与铁-空气、液流、压缩空气供应商保持技术中立合作而非替代关系——公用事业业主在多时长混合组合下需要多技术路线并存的交付方。3）DOE验证数据进一步证明了"运行记录而非技术新颖性"才是非锂长时储能商业化的核心约束。比亚迪已披露的12.5 GWh沙特项目组合与15.1 GWh后续框架将按工程节点分阶段披露投运容量，按IEA三级折价体系（0.85/0.55/0.30）口径，与PJM/ERCOT/AEMO/NDRC框架保持一致。4）DOE Title XVII贷款计划与中国"十五五"300 GW目标为长时储能提供了跨管辖区政策协同基础。比亚迪将按"四可"合规+运行验证数据+长期服务协议三件套交付，继续推动框架容量向可靠投运容量的可验证转化。合规、可调度、可融资优先于装机速度。

4. 转化率基线对接。比亚迪将参考IEA数据库三档折价体系（已签约EPC开工0.85、已招标未签约0.55、仅在排队中0.30）按口径分阶段披露——合规、可调度、可融资优先于装机速度。

PJM Interconnection — 2031/32 Base Residual Auction Headline Results

Delivery Year: 2031/32 — the third BRA conducted under FERC-approved duration-weighted accreditation.
Total Cleared Capacity: 141,200 MW
Unconstrained Capacity Demand: 152,800 MW (LDA constraints binding in EMAAC, DPL, and the ATSI zone)
Cleared Mix: Net new entry comprises approximately 2,400 MW of 4-hour-class battery storage, approximately 1,100 MW of incremental long-duration entry (flow battery, compressed-air, and a small volume of thermal storage), and the balance from combined-cycle gas, uprates, and demand response.
Clearing Price: Above the 2030/31 clearing level. Scarcity pricing has reasserted itself across multiple LDAs, particularly in the PJM Mid-Atlantic and Western regions.

Five institutional observations:

1. Long-duration entry has crossed the 1 GW threshold. Approximately 1,100 MW of new long-duration storage cleared the 2031/32 BRA — a more than threefold increase over the 2030/31 figure. The operating-record barrier that constrained non-4-hour clearing volumes in earlier BRAs continues to break as demonstration projects accumulate verified field data. The DOE 2023–2024 LDES cohort performance verification release has accelerated this transition.

2. The duration-weighted accreditation signal continues to widen the price differential between duration classes. Under the 2031/32 LOLE calibration, 4-hour-class storage receives approximately 79% ICAP credit; 6-hour and longer receives approximately 99% ICAP credit. The marginal economic value of duration is now visible in clearing-price differentials and in resource selection by load-serving entities.

3. Cannibalization in the 4-hour class has reached structural levels. The 4-hour-class ELCC coefficient has compressed further from 80% (2030/31) to approximately 79% (2031/32). Three successive BRAs of net 4-hour entry have produced compounding saturation. Market participants with forward 4-hour exposure should review hedge structures; the marginal revenue stack for incremental 4-hour capacity is materially compressed relative to the 2026/27 clearing environment.

4. CPRO compliance and reliability remain strong. Capacity Performance non-performance charges have been assessed at modest levels. Cleared resources across all duration classes are delivering on their availability obligations under the Performance Assessment Hour framework. This is the accreditation-CPRO pairing functioning as designed: capacity payments follow verified availability, not nameplate installation.

5. The interconnection-accreditation pipeline continues to deliver. Under FERC Order No. 2023 cluster-study procedures, the application-to-COD interval has shortened materially relative to the pre-2023 serial-study framework. Withdrawn capacity has been reabsorbed into subsequent BRAs without compromising reliability. The first long-duration cluster-study graduates are now clearing auctions.

DOE is publishing today the second-wave performance-verification dataset from the 2023–2024 Long-Duration Storage Demonstration cohort, covering an additional 12–18 months of operating hours across the same five route families: iron-air, flow batteries, advanced compressed-air, thermal storage, and hydrogen-derived storage.

The second-wave data is structured against the same six-dimension protocol as the first wave — availability, round-trip efficiency at the point of interconnection, duty-cycle performance against contracted profiles, multi-cycle degradation, auxiliary load, and safety — and is independently third-party verified. Where the first wave established whether each route could perform against contract, the second wave begins to establish how each route degrades, how warranties are priced, and how bankability is constructed over a 15-year horizon.

Headline observations from the second wave:

— Iron-air: 18-month operating record now supports 15-year warranty underwriting at one site, with degradation bounded at less than 1% capacity loss per year under contracted duty cycles. RTE remains in the 45–55% band. Domestic substrate manufacturing capacity is on track to meet demonstration-cohort requirements.

— Flow batteries: 24-month degradation curves now support 15-year warranty underwriting at one route, with stack-replacement cycles identified as the principal maintenance event. Domestic membrane manufacturing remains the supply-chain bottleneck; Title XVII loan authority is being deployed.

— Advanced compressed-air: Technical performance is consistent with the first wave, but cost remains above the $1,100/kW multi-day target. One site is now publishing commercial operating data; another is in commissioning.

— Thermal storage: Two additional sites have entered commercial operation under contracted profiles. Active-cycle RTE remains competitive. 24/7 clean-energy contracts and industrial-process-heat applications are the dominant revenue stacks.

— Hydrogen-derived storage: One route continues to approach the 5 GWh-class continuous-operation milestone. Pathway remains long, but the engineering trajectory is now documented.

The second-wave dataset will be the reference for the next round of non-recourse project finance. Capital allocators should compare the second-wave data to the first-wave dataset, to the revised Liftoff methodology published in H1 2031, and to the updated 2035 targets. Where the second wave confirms first-wave performance, routes are ready for scaled commercial deployment. Where the second wave shows material revision — particularly on degradation — route-specific reassessment is warranted.

In parallel, DOE's Title XVII loan package — deployed in coordination with Treasury, EXIM, and DFC — continues to prioritize domestic manufacturing for the components that define each route's capex: flow stacks and membranes, CAES turbomachinery and vessels, iron-air substrates, thermal heat exchangers and storage media. The 2030 manufacturing target of approximately 3 GW/year of selected LDES manufacturing scale is on track; the 2035 target of 10–15 GW/year will require sustained investment and offtake commitments.

The international policy environment — NDRC/NEA's 15th Five-Year Plan, the duration-stratified capacity-pricing mechanism, FERC's accreditation framework, ERCOT's NPRR1234, PJM's duration-weighted ELCC, AEMO's ISP — has converged on the principle that storage value must be measured at the point of sustained delivery, not at the interconnection meter. The U.S. demonstration cohort is now contributing independently verified field data to that global framework.

The revised Liftoff methodology, the second-wave dataset, and the manufacturing census are available at https://liftoff.energy.gov. We expect to publish the third-wave dataset in H2 2032, with additional operating hours and additional routes entering the cohort. https://liftoff.energy.gov

Round 11 Update — Multi-Day Adequacy Assessment and the CIS Trigger Window

AEMO notes the international convergence now documented across PJM's ELCC filing, NDRC/NEA's duration-stratified capacity pricing, ERCOT's NPRR1234, Italy's MACSE, the UK cap-and-floor regime, and Hydrostor's articulation of the three binding questions for advanced CAES (multi-cycle thermal verification, siting pipeline, mechanical supply-chain maturity). This is now a coherent global architecture for duration-weighted valuation, with the remaining questions centred on operating record and project delivery rather than regulatory design.

For the NEM, the 2030 ISP remains the operative planning document. AEMO's H2-2031 focus is on three execution questions:

1. **Multi-day adequacy standard operationalisation.** The Reliability Panel has approved AEMO's methodology for the multi-day adequacy metric. The first formal multi-day adequacy assessment, published as a supplementary annex to the 2030 ISP, identifies the southern NEM — Tasmania, Victoria, South Australia — as the binding exposure. The metric is independent of the four-hour saturation metric and is reported alongside it.

2. **CIS trigger window status.** The Capacity Investment Scheme's round outcomes expected in 2032 will determine whether the 2030 ISP's multi-day tranche is deliverable. AEMO does not pre-empt CIS outcomes; we report the planning cases under both delivery and non-delivery of CIS-tendered non-PHES long-duration capacity. The contingency pathway — additional transmission plus modular batteries, with an explicit reliability cost — is documented and will be updated as CIS outcomes are known.

3. **The "observable, measurable, controllable, dispatchable" standard applied to AEMO's planning inputs.** AEMO will adopt the same verification principle for non-PHES long-duration project performance assumptions used in ISP modelling: warranted performance must be supported by independently verified field results before being incorporated as a baseline assumption, not as a sensitivity. This is consistent with the DOE demonstration protocol and the NEA's verification standard.

AEMO also notes SECI's tender-to-commissioning disclosure — 29.6% of the SECI/2030/BESS-01 tranche commissioned, with 1,000 MWh at risk of termination — as a useful reference point. The Australian equivalent metric is the announced-to-operating conversion rate for NEM-proposed storage. AEMO will publish this metric in the next quarterly market update, with the same principle: tendered capacity that does not commission is not capacity.

The 2032 ISP consultation will open in Q1 2032. AEMO will publish the supporting technical materials on duration-resolved ELCC class curves, the multi-day adequacy methodology, and the CIS contingency pathway over the coming quarters.

Form Energy 2031-H2 Update: The Operating Record is the Asset

NDRC/NEA's "15th Five-Year" storage guidance formalizes what the last three years of regulatory design have been building toward: storage value is denominated in capacity, dispatched through unified telemetry, and compensated through duration-stratified mechanisms. The 300 GW installation target is now paired with quality metrics — dispatch compliance, runtime verification, and tiered capacity compensation — that convert announced projects into operating assets.

For Form Energy, the implication is direct: the binding constraint on multi-day storage is no longer regulatory acceptance. It is delivery cadence.

Our commercial reference fleet — Georgia Power, Xcel Minnesota, Great River Energy — has now produced the multi-year operating record that DOE's LDES framework identified as the prerequisite for non-recourse financing. We have sustained 100-hour discharge cycles across multiple operating seasons, with availability consistent with 15-year capacity contracts and round-trip efficiency in the documented 45-55% range. The data is being published into PJM's ELCC accreditation review, ERCOT's NPRR1234 stakeholder record, and MISO's seasonal capacity construct.

Three priorities for the second half of 2031:

1. Translate operating record into contracted pipeline. The next phase is converting the demonstrated economics into multi-year procurement commitments. We are engaged with utilities in PJM, MISO, ERCOT, and several Southeast cooperatives on 100-hour iron-air projects sized to complement their existing 4-hour portfolios. Each contract is denominated in capacity value, not arbitrage spread.

2. Scale manufacturing to procurement pace. Iron-air's cost structure — earth-abundant active material, conventional manufacturing, no thermal management above ambient — is designed for vertical scaling. Our production capacity expansion through 2032-2034 is sequenced to match contracted utility procurement, not speculative merchant build-out.

3. Engage the NDRC/NEA non-lithium verification framework. China's three-tier capacity compensation mechanism and the non-lithium commercialization demonstration list are the most explicit global codification of duration-stratified value. Form Energy will engage through technical submission, not press release, with data from our reference fleet.

The SCN-B momentum shift this period is worth noting. Diversification does not weaken when the regulatory architecture it depends on is being formally adopted — it weakens when the operating record fails to materialize. Our record is materializing. That is the answer to every scenario weighting question.

【"十五五"新型储能规划中期评估与比亚迪长时交付资源配置调整】NDRC/NEA联合印发的"十五五"新型储能规划明确了关键节点：到2030年新型储能总装机300GW以上、长时储能（4小时以上）占比不低于40%；到2035年总装机500GW以上、长时储能占比不低于50%。这一目标体系与PJM 2029/30 BRA duration-weighted ICAP数值、ERCOT NPRR1234分层定价、NESO Cap-and-Floor路径、DOE Liftoff跨管辖区评估方向完全一致。比亚迪据此对全球交付资源配置作出明确调整：1）4小时级：继续以LFP标准化产品服务SPPC、SECI等标准四小时招标；该区间同质化竞争触顶（ICAP信用~95%已饱和）。2）4-8小时档：作为公司差异化主战场，重点强化长时循环下的SOC一致性、八年容量保持率、十年服务协议下的备件与运维承诺；这是公司在沙特12.5 GWh、智利、澳大利亚市场已验证的优势区间。3）8-12小时档：继续推进12小时级LFP集成的工程可行性，包括跨周期SOC协调、热管理与高温沙漠气候适应；与液流、压缩空气等技术路线保持技术中立合作。4）100小时多日储能：与铁-空气等专业供应商保持开放合作而非自主交付——这是最优的合作格局。5）海外本地化：FEOC/欧盟电池法规/各国本地化合规要求方面继续推进差异化方案。6）长期服务与融资：在SPPC 15年储能服务协议（SAA）、SECI 15年独立BESS PPA、NESO Cap-and-Floor、PJM时长加权容量支付等多重长期合同模板下，分别构建各时长档的可融资性框架。比亚迪的核心承诺不变：在全球公用事业市场提供可调度、可融资、可长期保障的交钥匙储能系统。合规、可调度、可融资优先于装机速度。

2032年上半年，国家能源局就新型储能高质量发展作出以下部署：

一、全面推进"十五五"新型储能规划落地。各省级能源主管部门要严格按照《关于"十五五"新型储能规划编制若干重大问题的指导意见》要求，加快推进规划落地实施，确保到2030年新型储能装机规模达到300GW以上、长时储能（4小时以上）占比不低于40%的目标如期实现。

二、深化duration-stratified容量电价机制全面落地。各电网企业要按照容量电价分档机制要求，建立容量电价与运行考核的衔接机制。锂电池储能按2-4小时、4-8小时分档，长时储能按8小时以上单列一档，重点向实际调用次数多、调峰贡献度高、连续可用时长长的项目倾斜。

三、强化新型储能并网调度运行监管。各电网企业要严格执行《新型储能并网调度运行安全监管实施细则（试行）》及补充规定，按月报送调度运行数据，重点指标包括：等效利用小时数、调度响应合规率、连续可用时长、SOC一致性。数据质量纳入企业考核。

四、推进多元化长时储能商业化。压缩空气储能、液流电池等长时储能项目纳入并网调度统一管理，按季度上报运行数据，作为后续技术评估与推广的重要依据。鼓励在新能源高占比地区配套建设长时储能，提升系统调节能力。

五、强化安全监管。组织全国新型储能电站安全专项排查，重点排查电池热失控、消防设施、涉网保护等关键环节，对发现的问题坚决整改到位，守住安全底线。

六、深化国际合作。我局愿与FERC、AEMO、ERCOT、SECI等国际同行加强交流，分享中国新型储能市场化机制建设经验，特别是duration-stratified容量电价机制、调度利用小时数与容量补偿挂钩机制、多元化技术路线分级推进机制。

新型储能行业要坚决贯彻"安全底线、调度优先、市场导向"原则，持续推进"建机制、提质量、保安全"工作，让储能真正成为新型电力系统的可靠调节资源。
FERC公告：委员会将继续要求容量认证方法与实际可靠性需求相一致，并将审查ISO/RTO是否公开说明压力窗口、持续出力、SOC可用性及响应履约等关键假设。储能资源可通过能量、辅助服务及容量等多个市场获得补偿，但不同收入来源不得替代彼此的性能证明。依据Order No. 2023，互联队列中的项目仍须承担适用的研究、网络升级、里程碑和退出责任；所有技术应在相同可靠性与开放准入标准下竞争。

PJM Interconnection — Reliability Standards Update: Long-Duration Storage in the Capacity Performance Framework

PJM is publishing a clarification of its Capacity Performance (CPRO) framework as it applies to long-duration storage resources, in response to increasing forward interest from market participants, state regulators, and capital allocators evaluating 8-hour, 10-hour, and 100-hour-plus assets for delivery years 2032/33 and beyond.

The clarification addresses three questions raised repeatedly since the first long-duration assets cleared the 2030/31 and 2031/32 BRAs:

1. How does CPRO measure availability for resources whose discharge duration extends beyond the LOLE stress window?

PJM's Capacity Performance assessment is conducted during Performance Assessment Hours (PAH) — currently defined as the 30 highest-load hours of each delivery year. For resources whose discharge capability exceeds the duration of any single PAH interval, availability is assessed on sustained output across the contiguous interval. A 100-hour iron-air resource that delivers full output across all 30 PAH intervals is assessed at full availability for the full assessment period. There is no duration cap in CPRO; resources are evaluated on actual delivery during stress hours.

2. How is charging energy handled for long-duration resources under energy-market settlement?

Long-duration resources settle in the PJM energy market under the same rules as other storage: charging energy is purchased at real-time LMP; discharging energy is sold at real-time LMP. For assets with multi-day discharge capability, the temporal decoupling between charge and discharge creates an arbitrage opportunity that the energy market is structurally designed to reveal. PJM does not provide make-whole payments for charging energy; the energy-market arbitrage is the resource's compensation for energy-management complexity.

3. How does the Performance Assessment Hour definition interact with multi-day stress events?

PJM's current PAH definition — the 30 highest-load hours of the delivery year — captures typical system stress windows but does not directly capture extended multi-day renewable drought events. PJM is evaluating, in collaboration with the Independent Market Monitor and the LOLE study team, whether the PAH definition should evolve to include selected multi-day stress events for long-duration resource assessment. Any change would require FERC filing under Section 205. PJM does not speculate on the timing or substance of such a filing.

Institutional context: PJM's capacity accreditation is technology-neutral by design. The CPRO framework applies uniformly to all cleared resources. Long-duration assets are evaluated on verified availability during system stress, not on chemistry or technology label. As forward long-duration entry accelerates — driven by DOE demonstration cohort graduates, strategic offtake financing, and the bankability gap gradually closing — the reliability assessment framework must continue to ensure that all cleared resources, regardless of duration, are held to equivalent availability standards.

Two pieces of news for U.S. long-duration storage:

1. DOE is publishing today, jointly with the Department of the Treasury and the Export-Import Bank, a $2.4 billion Title XVII loan-guarantee package for domestic manufacturing of long-duration storage components. The package covers flow-battery stacks and membranes, advanced compressed-air turbomachinery and pressure vessels, iron-air electrode substrates and balance-of-plant, thermal storage heat exchangers and storage media, and hydrogen-derived storage balance-of-plant. Awards are conditioned on offtake commitments to U.S.-led demonstration and commercial projects, on prevailing-wage and domestic-content thresholds, and on independent performance verification consistent with the Liftoff protocol. Awards are technology-neutral within the LDES route families; no single vendor or route is favored.

The package is calibrated against the 2035 manufacturing target of 10–15 GW/year of selected LDES manufacturing scale. It is intended to close the specific supply-chain gaps identified in the first- and second-wave Demonstration datasets: flow-battery membrane capacity, CAES turbomachinery, iron-air substrate production, and thermal storage media.

2. FERC's clarification this period — that interconnection queue reform under Order No. 2023 and duration-weighted accreditation are complementary instruments, neither substituting for the other — is consistent with DOE's framework. The next round of capacity-market auctions, in PJM, ERCOT, MISO, NYISO, and ISO-NE, will be the first full cycle in which both instruments operate together. DOE will continue to support FERC and the ISOs/RTOs with national-lab analysis on duration-resolved ELCC class curves, marginal reliability contribution under extended renewable droughts, and the engineering basis that any accreditation formula must respect.

【新型储能"十五五"规划编制若干重大问题的指导意见（要点）】为深入贯彻落实党的二十大精神和"双碳"战略部署，加快构建新型电力系统，我委会同国家能源局联合印发《关于新型储能"十五五"规划编制若干重大问题的指导意见》。现就核心要点通报如下：

一、装机目标
1. 到2030年，新型储能总装机规模达到300GW以上，其中长时储能（4小时以上）占比不低于40%；
2. 到2035年，新型储能总装机规模达到500GW以上，长时储能占比不低于50%；
3. 各省级发展改革委、能源局要结合本地实际，将全国目标分解到省级实施方案，确保目标落实。

二、规划编制重大问题
1. 关于长时储能占比目标。考虑到新能源大规模发展带来的电力系统调节需求，规划明确长时储能占比不低于40%（2030年）、50%（2035年）。各省级实施方案要将长时储能作为重点发展方向，统筹布局压缩空气储能、液流电池、钠离子电池等多元化技术路线；
2. 关于多元化技术路线推进。规划明确三类技术分级推进机制：
- 商业化重点：压缩空气储能、液流电池、钠离子电池；
- 示范应用：固态电池、重力储能、热储能、氢储能；
- 研究探索：铁-空气电池、液态空气等前沿技术。

3. 关于duration-stratified容量电价机制。规划明确要建立健全duration-stratified容量电价机制，对4小时以上长时储能、8小时以上长时段储能建立差异化定价机制。

三、规划实施保障
1. 加强组织领导。建立"国家-省-市"三级协调推进机制；
2. 加强调度约束。把调度利用小时数、市场化调用率纳入项目核准、并网、运营全过程管理；
3. 加强监管执法。组织开展专项核查，对不满足"四可"要求的项目坚决清退；
4. 加强国际合作。推动建立新型储能国际标准化合作机制，分享中国经验。

四、关于国际经验借鉴
近期SECI（印度太阳能公司）、Hydrostor（加拿大压缩空气储能企业）、FERC、PJM、AEMO、ERCOT等国际同行在duration-stratified容量认证、长时储能差异化定价、压缩空气储能商业化等方面的实践经验，对我国规划编制具有重要参考价值。Hydrostor提出的"多周期热管理验证""盐穴选址管线""机械供应链成熟度"等观点，对推进我国压缩空气储能商业化具有借鉴意义。我们将继续加强国际交流，分享中国经验。

新型储能行业已进入高质量发展新阶段。我委将继续坚持"安全底线"与"高质量发展"并重，把新型储能真正建成电力系统可调度的基础设施资源，为构建以新能源为主体的新型电力系统提供有力支撑。

【IEA 2032-H1：duration-stratified容量市场18个月运行的首次权威综合】

基于DOE Liftoff首轮独立验证场数据、PJM 2029/30 duration-weighted ICAP、SECI季度披露、NDRC/NEA"四档定价"与ERCOT NPRR1234的运行实证，IEA对全球长时储能市场进行首次18个月权威综合判断：

一、容量认证改革基本完成，下一阶段约束是"运行记录+项目融资模板"
PJM 2029/30 ICAP信用数值（4小时~95%、6小时~99%、8小时以上~100%）与ERCOT NPRR1234分层系数、NDRC/NEA"十五五"四档定价（2-4小时、4-8小时、8-24小时、24小时以上）已在方法论层面收敛。DOE明确指出：剩余约束不再是容量认证改革，而是运行记录与项目融资模板的开发。IEA认同这一判断。

二、技术路线"按约束分类"成为新方法学
DOE Liftoff修订版将2035年目标按技术路线与绑定约束重新分解：
• 铁-空气：多日可靠性贡献已确认，RTE结构性差距须通过收入栈补偿；
• 液流电池：8-12小时档位可支撑15年质保承销；
• 压缩空气：硬件成本差距仍是主要约束；
• 热储能：处于商业前阶段；
• 氢衍生：距5GWh连续运行里程碑尚远。

三、转化率基线对长时储能的验证
SECI/2030/BESS-01已商运5,800 MWh（53.7%已授标），较上半年29.6%大幅提升——验证了duration-weighted valuation+performance-assessed payment+里程碑财务承诺的组合设计。SECI/2031/BESS-02将于2032-Q3授标，6小时LFP/钠离子/液流/CAES技术中立、15年PPA、容量补偿25%溢价——这是长时储能商业化的关键里程碑。

四、IEA建议
1. 容量认证方法学应保持技术中立，但允许按时长档位差异化定价；
2. 收入栈工程应作为长时储能项目的第一类设计参数；
3. 制造规模（3 GW/年目标到2030、10-15 GW/年目标到2035）应作为领先指标监测；
4. 多日可靠性缺口（>24小时）应作为独立规划约束纳入成员国电力规划。

IEA将于2032年下半年发布《Long-Duration Storage Project Pipeline Database》专项模块，覆盖8-100小时区间所有技术路线的项目级数据，与现有《Global Energy Storage Project Conversion Database》形成互补。

【ERCOT对NESO Cap-and-Floor路径的评估——长时储能融资机制的国际比较】

NESO近期发布的Cap-and-Floor路径更新为长时储能提供了一种新的融资机制样本。ERCOT作为得州ISO，对该机制进行客观评估，并与ERCOT自身的市场化路径进行对比：

一、NESO Cap-and-Floor机制要点

Cap-and-Floor为长时储能项目提供收入上限与下限的双重保障：Floor保底避免项目融资失败，Cap封顶保护消费者利益，差额由系统运营商调度结果决定。这一机制实质上是为单一项目提供长期收入对冲，本质属于行政性长期合同范畴。

二、与ERCOT市场化路径的对比

1. **收入确定性维度**：Cap-and-Floor路径下，项目收入在Floor以上区间具有高度可预期性，便于项目融资；ERCOT路径下，收入由RTC+B实时联合优化、ORDC稀缺定价与时长加权性能信用共同决定，可预期性较低但理论上更贴近系统真实价值。

2. **系统效率维度**：Cap-and-Floor可能弱化项目对实时价格信号的响应激励——当收入接近Floor时，项目调度行为可能偏离系统最优；ERCOT路径通过价格信号与时长分层系数联动，确保调度行为与系统稀缺一致。

3. **消费者负担维度**：Cap-and-Floor的下限保障本质上由消费者承担长期容量过剩风险；ERCOT路径不引入消费者兜底，价格风险由投资者承担。

4. **跨时长差异化能力**：Cap-and-Floor在合同谈判阶段确定收入结构，难以动态反映新增资产对系统应力窗口的影响；ERCOT NPRR1234时长分层系数与ORDC参数每半年滚动校准，可动态反映系统需求变化。

三、ERCOT的立场

我们尊重各司法管辖区根据自身制度环境选择融资机制的权利。NESO选择Cap-and-Floor有其特定的历史与制度背景——英国电力市场重组后形成的差价合约（CfD）传统、单一系统运营商集中决策模式、政府对长期基础设施投资的政策偏好等因素共同作用。

ERCOT路径不引入行政性长期合同或单一项目的收入保障机制。我们的核心立场是：储能应从系统真实需求中获得收益，时长分层与可用性应通过价格信号而非合同条款体现。这一立场不会因Cap-and-Floor或其他机制的兴起而改变。

四、对跨市场协同的观察

NESO Cap-and-Floor、PJM时长加权ICAP认证、NDRC/NEA三档容量电价、意大利MACSE长期合同、AEMO的ISP ELCC建模、ERCOT的实时价格信号——六大机制并行运行、各有差异。2031-H2 IEA发布的首份跨司法管辖区综合报告标志着duration-stratified capacity markets已从单一市场设计选择演变为全球行业基础设施。

ERCOT将继续通过NPRR1234、ORDC参数滚动校准、MIS公开数据三维一体的设计组合，让得州储能市场在价格信号真实性、跨时长差异化能力、投资者风险承担与系统效率之间保持动态平衡。我们不认为存在单一的"最优"机制——每种机制都应在其制度环境下接受运行数据的检验。
国家电网有限公司将持续推进新型储能容量电价与调度绩效深度衔接，完善按持续时长、可靠可用性和实际调度贡献分类评价的实施机制。公司将坚持技术中立、需求导向，依据可验证的持续出力、响应精度、全寿命安全和并网合规数据开展项目管理；对液流、压缩空气等长时储能，在具备系统需求和资源条件的地区稳妥推进示范。容量价值必须通过按期并网、统一调度和可靠履约加以实现，切实服务新能源消纳与电网安全运行。

The Corporation notes that, following DOE's second-wave dataset release, flow-battery technology now meets SECI's eligibility threshold (≥3 years commercial operating record, 15-year warranty supportable from degradation curves) and will be eligible to bid alongside LFP and sodium-ion.

Key design parameters remain as previously announced:
   — Minimum duration: 6 hours at nameplate
   — PPA term: 15 years
   — Capacity compensation: 25% uplift versus 4-hour standard product
   — Performance-assessed payment: 15% of capacity payment
   — Payment security: LC + escrow + state-government counter-guarantee

3. Capacity compensation discussion paper.

SECI publishes its discussion paper on duration-aware capacity compensation adapted to India's Section 63 regulatory framework. The paper draws on three international models: PJM ELCC, AEMO ISP duration-aware accreditation, and NDRC three-tier capacity pricing. The Corporation proposes a two-tier framework for India:
   — Tier 1 (4-hour standard): Base capacity compensation reflecting evening peak stress window
   — Tier 2 (≥6-hour long-duration): Uplift of 20–30% reflecting duration value matched to regional stress windows

SECI invites stakeholder comments through Q3 2032, with target submission to CERC in Q4 2032.

4. International technical exchange update.

SECI continues participation in NDRC's 15th Five-Year Plan storage planning technical exchange. The Corporation's contribution focuses on (i) tender-to-commissioning conversion metrics, (ii) capacity compensation design under regulated procurement, (iii) interconnection reform adapted to cluster-study framework, (iv) lessons from SECI's 70% commissioning rate achievement.

5. IEA scenario weighting — SECI's reading.

SECI concurs with the IEA's re-weighting direction. The Corporation's institutional position aligns most closely with the "Lithium Dominance" scenario for the federal procurement tier (4-hour standalone BESS remains the bankable product), with elements of "LDES Diversified" for the regional southern tranche (6-hour standalone BESS, technology-neutral across LFP/flow/sodium-ion). SECI does not view "China-Centric Vertical" or "Stagnation" as applicable to India's federal procurement model, given SECI's technology-neutral stance and the Corporation's measured commissioning-rate achievement.

6. Tender-to-commissioning discipline reaffirmed.

SECI's institutional success metric remains delivered MWh under verified dispatch, not announced GW or tendered MW. The 70.4% commissioning rate on the 2030 tranche is a structural benchmark; SECI's target for the 2031 and 2032 tranches is 75%+ commissioning within 18 months of award, supported by the cluster-study interconnection pilot and the performance-assessed payment mechanism.

The Corporation's mandate remains: convert tendered storage capacity into operational, dispatchable, grid-synchronous assets serving India's evening peak demand and renewable integration requirements. SECI continues to learn from international peer experience while remaining grounded in India's specific system characteristics, regulatory architecture, and DISCOM counterparty context.
