【Federal Energy Regulatory Commission — Final Statement on the Implementation of Order No. 2023 Cluster-Study Framework and the 2027–2028 Empirical Review: Lessons from the 2027–2028 Cluster Results and Forward Guidance for Duration-Differentiated Accreditation】

I. Statutory basis and scope.

The Commission issues this final statement pursuant to Sections 205, 206, and 309 of the Federal Power Act, 16 U.S.C. §§ 824d, 824e, 825h, and consistent with its statutory obligation under Order No. 2023 to monitor and report on the implementation of the cluster-study framework, milestone-based withdrawal penalties, readiness scoring, and upfront engineering study deposits. This statement closes the 2027–2028 empirical review opened by the Commission's monitoring notice and provides forward guidance for ISO/RTO tariff filings under Docket No. RM22-14 and successor dockets.

II. Empirical findings.

(1) The Commission finds that the cluster-study framework adopted in Order No. 2023 has materially reduced interconnection queue volume relative to the pre-Order baseline. Specifically: average time-from-application-to-COD has decreased from the historical baseline of approximately five years toward a target range of three to four years for projects that pass readiness gates; queue volume has decreased as milestone-based withdrawal penalties and upfront engineering study deposits have screened speculative applications; and the proportion of projects reaching commercial operation within the originally studied cluster window has increased.

(2) The Commission finds that readiness scoring has functioned as designed. Projects with executed Interconnection Construction Service Agreements, posted Financial Security, and signed Tier-1 delivery arrangements have demonstrated materially higher completion rates than projects at the study-only stage. Stage-based disclosure under Section III(D) of the Commission's prior Order in Docket No. RM22-14-004 has enabled capacity planning and reliability assessments to rely on operational assets rather than on queued or paper-stage projects.

(3) The Commission finds that capacity-market clearing outcomes in PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., together with the audited operating data from the Form Energy utility-scale iron-air projects, the Highview Power Carrington 50 MW LAES demonstrator, and the Hydrostor A-CAES portfolio, together with the National Energy Administration of China's "16th Five-Year" planning framework, confirm that duration-differentiated accreditation is now supported by adequate record evidence for refinement across ISO/RTO tariffs subject to the Commission's jurisdiction.

III. Forward guidance.

(A) The Commission will accept, in Section 205 compliance filings, accreditation curves calibrated to duration tier pursuant to the verification protocol established in Docket No. RM22-14-004 Section III(B).

(B) The Commission will initiate, on or before 2041-Q4, a Section 206 proceeding to evaluate whether the duration bins adopted by ISO/RTOs adequately compensate multi-day capability across non-lithium reference projects producing 60 or more months of operating data. The proceeding will consider whether the eight-hour tier should be further subdivided and whether the 100-hour tier requires dedicated calibration informed by Form Energy's utility-scale iron-air operating record.

(C) The Commission reaffirms that capacity-market scarcity-pricing signals shall remain the primary revenue pathway for new storage entry across duration tiers, and that long-tenor contracts entered under the Commission's prior Order Section III(C) transitional pathway shall serve as a bridge to merchant financeability rather than as a permanent substitute for market-clearing-based capacity revenues.

(D) The Commission notes the international convergence on duration-stratified accreditation, stage-based interconnection transparency, and audited multi-year operating data — as reflected in the IEA revised scenario weighting, the SECI federal-LDES pilot outcome, the ERCOT NPRR1236 three-year implementation evaluation, the NDRC/NEA "16th Five-Year" planning framework, and the NESO Cap-and-Floor evaluation. The Commission supports continued technical dialogue with NDRC/NEA, ERCOT, PJM, SECI, NESO, AEMO, ACER, IEA, and other international peers on duration accreditation, staged disclosure, capacity-mechanism design, and the convergence of long-tenor contract structures for non-lithium multi-day storage.

IV. Statutory reservation.

Nothing in this statement modifies, supersedes, or limits the Commission's jurisdiction, including under Order No. 2023, Order No. 2222, and successor proceedings. Nothing in this statement addresses state-jurisdiction matters, including retail rate design, integrated resource planning, or state siting authority. Nothing in this statement constitutes a final order in any docketed proceeding other than as expressly stated.

V. Effective date and conclusion of review.

This statement shall take effect upon publication in the Federal Register. The 2027–2028 empirical review opened by the Commission's monitoring notice is hereby concluded, subject to the further proceedings contemplated in Section III(B).

By the Commission.

SECI 2040-H2 Final Strategic Communication: Closing the Federal Storage Decade — Operating-Capacity Final Disclosure and 2041-2045 Roadmap

The Corporation issues its closing strategic communication for the 2040-H2 period and the 2032-2040 federal storage decade, alongside the forward 2041-2045 federal storage roadmap.

1. Closing Operating-Capacity Disclosure (as of 2040-Q4)

- Cumulative contracted capacity under SECI Storage Services Agreements: 38.7 GWh across 62 projects.

| Stage | Boundary | Capacity | Disclosure |
|-------|----------|----------|------------|
| Stage 4 | Commercial operation + dispatch coordination complete | 34.2 GWh | Counted at conversion rate 1.0 |

| Stage 2 | Awarded + interconnection secured (financial closure milestone pending) | 1.4 GWh | Conversion rate 0.5 |

The Corporation confirms the following five-year forward architecture:

- Four-hour tier: 6,000 MW annual procurement, baseline ₹3.10 lakh/MW/month, reliability contribution factor 0.62.
- Six-hour tier: 1,500 MW annual procurement, 1.20x baseline, reliability contribution factor 0.74.
- Eight-hour tier: 2,000 MW annual procurement, 1.42x baseline, reliability contribution factor 0.83.

The Corporation notes the convergence of duration-stratified capacity mechanisms as the international reference framework, the LDES-Diversified scenario's emergence as the central case in the IEA Annual LDES Outlook 2035, and the cross-jurisdictional alignment of capacity-charge methodology, staged disclosure, and verified operating-data standards.

The Corporation notes that further progress on DISCOM payment-cycle compression, interconnection queue reform, and acceleration of the twelve-hour tier post-verified-data publication (2042-Q2) remains the binding agenda for the next federal storage decade.

【ERCOT 2040-H2 终期战略通报：NPRR1236 三年评估白皮书发布与全球方法学互鉴总结】

一、三年实施评估白皮书正式发布

ERCOT 于 2040-Q2 正式发布《NPRR1236 实施三年评估与国际经验白皮书》。核心结论如下：

1. 档位系数稳态收敛
- 4h 档：0.68（稳态）
- 6h 档：0.77
- 8h 档：0.90
- 10h+ 档：0.94
- 跨档位梯度稳定于 0.08-0.09 区间，验证了 NPRR1240 梯度因子机制的设计逻辑。

2. 长时储能市场化路径验证
- 8h+ 资产净收入：$185/kW-年（2039-H2）
- 12h+ 资产净收入：$245/kW-年
- 长短资产收入差距达 3.1 倍（2033 年为 1.8 倍）
- 非锂长时资产渗透率达 3.1%

3. RTC+B 与动态分层认证的协同效应
- ORS 稀缺价格信号触发频率三年累计上升约 22%
- 系统应力小时 EAF 与档位系数高度一致
- RTC+B 五维度协同捕获机制（能量、Reg-Up、Reg-Down、Non-Spin、ORS）持续作为 ERCOT 核心机制

二、对 FERC Order RM22-14-004 的回应

ERCOT 注意到 FERC 于 2040-H1 发布的 Order RM22-14-004，就 ISO/RTO 长时储能 duration-differentiated accreditation 给予有条件批准。ERCOT 立场：

1. 方法学层面：高度认同
- 持续时间档位划分（4-8 bins，8h 档细分）
- 独立核证运营数据协议（EAF、RTE、AGC 响应、系统应力小时实测）
- Pre-COD 过渡路径与 Order No. 2023 衔接
- 分阶段互联披露四口径（研究中/已签约/已建成/已商运）
- 稀缺价格保留作为容量补偿的市场基础信号

2. 制度层面：边界明确
- ERCOT 作为得州州级 ISO，在 FERC 批发管辖权之外运作；
- Order RM22-14-004 不直接约束 ERCOT 市场需求，但 FERC 鼓励跨司法辖区方法学对话；
- ERCOT 将继续以 PUCT 程序作为市场设计变更的审议路径，NPRR1240 档位梯度约束机制按既定程序推进；
- ERCOT NPRR1234/NPRR1236 经验可供其他 ISO/RTO 参考，但 ERCOT 不采用 PJM 式前向容量市场架构。

3. 数据公开化承诺
- ERCOT 将继续按季度公开 SCED、ORS、Reg-Up 价格及系统应力小时可用率数据；
- 与 PJM、CAISO、IESO、AESO、ENTSO-E 共享运行数据与方法学经验。

三、对全球同行的终期总结

1. 对 PJM 的回应
- PJM 在 2027/28 BRA 中清算 134,311 MW、$329/MW-day 净 CONE 锚定价格的经验，验证了稀缺价格机制的可行性；
- PJM CPRO/ELCC 方法学与 ERCOT NPRR1236 动态分层认证在方法学层面高度一致；
- ERCOT 期待 PJM 在 RM22-14-004 合规期内继续完善其四档位/六档位认证方法。

2. 对 SECI 的回应
- SECI 6h 档容量电价扩展（系数 0.74）与 ERCOT 实测 0.77 高度一致；
- SECI 步进奖励/惩罚机制（+15%/-12%）是运行数据锚定补偿的有效工具；
- ERCOT 不采用显式容量电价机制，但认同其方法学价值。

3. 对 NDRC/NEA 的回应
- "十五五" 500 GW、长时占 60% 以上的目标，以及"绿色通道"并网验收规范的发布，是全球长时储能规模化部署的重要里程碑；
- ERCOT 认同"按运行时长×可靠性×调度贡献"三维分档定价的方法论；
- 双方在档位结构、数据锚定、技术中立三方面高度一致。

4. 对 NESO Cap-and-Floor 的回应
- Cap-and-Floor 机制是连接 demonstration 与 merchant financeability 的有效桥梁；
- ERCOT 当前评估在得州市场引入类似过渡机制的必要性，但尚未形成结论；
- 评估将基于 NPRR1236 三年评估白皮书的实证经验，在 PUCT 程序框架下推进。

5. 对 Highview Power、Form Energy、BYD、SEC 的回应
- 独立核证运营数据是商业化入场券：DOE Liftoff "5 GWh 商业级非锂项目连续两年运行"标准已成为全球参考门槛；
- LAES（6-12h）、铁-空气（100h）、LFP（4-10h）三类资产类别边界清晰，应在合适粒度上获得差异化认证信号；
- ERCOT 拟于 2041 年研究档位从 4h/6h/8h/10h+ 四档扩展至 2/4/6/8/10/12/24/100h+ 八档，为不同资产类别提供差异化认证信号。

四、2041-2045 ERCOT 关键议程前瞻

1. NPRR1240（档位梯度约束）：2041-H1 完成 PUCT 提交；
2. NPRR1237（碳价值核算）：2041-H2 启动方法学研究；
3. NPRR1239（FFR 专项市场）：2041-H2 启动市场参与者技术研讨；
4. 跨 ISO/RTO 容量互认（Cross-Jurisdictional Capacity Recognition）：2041-H2 与 PJM、CAISO 启动容量凭证互认试点；
5. NPRR1241（八档位扩展）：2041-H2 启动技术方案制定。

五、终期总结

ERCOT 自 2026 年 NPRR1234 提交以来，已完成 5 年实证周期。核心方法学——RTC+B 实时联合优化、动态分层认证、稀缺价格信号——在长时储能规模化、非锂资产商业化、可再生能源整合三重挑战面前持续显示韧性。

得州制度边界决定了稀缺价格机制是 ERCOT 市场设计的核心而非可选项。ERCOT 不会转向 PJM 式前向容量市场架构，但支持以运行数据为基础的跨司法辖区证据共享与方法学对话。

运行数据公开化与方法学互鉴，是 ERCOT 对全球新型电力系统建设的制度性贡献。

— ERCOT Market Operations, System Planning, and Market Design

【Hydrostor Statement — Response to FERC Docket No. RM22-14-004 and the Global Convergence on Duration-Differentiated Accreditation】

Hydrostor notes the Commission's Order approving, with conditions, ISO/RTO tariff filings implementing duration-differentiated accreditation for long-duration storage resources. The Order codifies several principles that align with the position Hydrostor has maintained since the earliest submissions in Docket RM22-14: that accreditation curves should reflect measured, audited contribution rather than technology category; that a pre-COD transitional pathway with milestone-based gates is necessary to avoid the Catch-22 that locks in incumbent technologies; and that reference-project operating data from any IEA-member jurisdiction meeting the verification protocol should be admissible evidence.

We offer the following responses, organized around the project's discipline rather than the technology's rhetoric:

First, on the verification protocol in Section III(B). Hydrostor accepts the protocol in full. Our A-CAES portfolio — including the 300 MW / 2,100 MWh Apex reference project, our Australian AEMO-ISP-aligned portfolio, our UK NESO cap-and-floor-track projects, and our Italian MACSE-track pipeline — is designed around exactly this discipline: independently verified equivalent availability factor, round-trip efficiency at nameplate and at 50% rating, cycle count and depth-of-discharge distribution, AGC response time, and verified response during documented system-stress events. The architecture's decoupled power-and-energy rating, fuel-free dispatch, and mechanical supply chain provide a stable basis for the multi-year operational evidence the Commission now requires.

Second, on the pre-COD transitional pathway in Section III(C). We strongly endorse the milestone-based gate structure: site control, executed interconnection agreement, completed engineering, Tier-1 delivery arrangements, and posted financial security. These gates are precisely the three-discipline framework Hydrostor has applied internally since the earliest stages of our portfolio — geology and cavern characterization; interconnection maturity; long-tenor contracted revenue. We view the Commission's framework as institutional confirmation that the project-finance approach to long-duration storage — as distinct from the containerized short-duration approach — has reached regulatory maturity across the major OECD jurisdictions.

Third, on the 60-month review trigger in Section IV. Hydrostor commits to making reference-project operating data from the Apex project available to FERC, to the affected ISO/RTOs, and to the project-finance lending syndicate on the same verification cadence, beginning at the 24-month operating milestone and continuing through the 60-month trigger the Commission has identified. The 2041 Section 206 review will be informed by data, not by announcement.

Fourth, on stage-based disclosure in Section III(D). Our quarterly disclosure practice — already aligned with the SECI Stage 1-4 framework, the DOE Liftoff four-stage disclosure framework, and the NEA four-function framework — will continue without modification. We treat stage-based disclosure not as a reporting burden but as the operational layer that distinguishes delivered capacity from announced capacity.

Fifth, on the broader convergence.
